renewable.plain_thesis: We think India keeps adding renewable capacity year after year, which helps the power producers, grid companies and equipment makers behind it. Across 32 past 1-year windows, an equal bundle of those names beat the Nifty more often than not — though the edge is modest, and a market-wide fall still drags the bundle down.
renewable.description: We think India keeps adding renewable capacity year after year, which helps the power producers, grid companies and equipment makers behind it. Across 32 past 1-year windows, an equal bundle of those names beat the Nifty more often than not — though the edge is modest, and a market-wide fall still drags the bundle down.
bullets: What drives it: India's renewable-capacity build-out lifts power & equipment firms.
How to act: own an equal bundle of 9 such companies for a year.
Main caveat: if the whole market falls, the bundle usually falls too.

yes.summary: If capacity keeps being added year after year, the producers, grid firms and equipment makers behind it tend to rise together.

no.summary: If the build-out slows, these names likely track the market — broad equity exposure is the steadier bet.

renewable.caveat: The wider power theme has historically barely beaten the market — treat it as a narrative, not a proven edge.

gold.plain_thesis: We looked at 19 real stretches when gold ran to new highs. In the 3 months after each, an equal bundle of jewellers and gold-loan firms earned about +8% on average and beat the Nifty in 84% of them. The catch: gold can pull back sharply, and the bundle goes with it.
gold.description: We looked at 19 real stretches when gold ran to new highs. In the 3 months after each, an equal bundle of jewellers and gold-loan firms earned about +8% on average and beat the Nifty in 84% of them. The catch: gold can pull back sharply, and the bundle goes with it.
bullets: What drives it: rising gold lifts jewellers and gold-loan firms.
How to act: own a bundle of 4 gold-linked firms (or a gold bet).
Main caveat: gold can pull back sharply, dragging the bundle.

yes.summary: If gold keeps climbing, jewellers, gold-loan financiers and gold itself tend to rise together.

no.summary: If gold stalls instead, gold-linked stocks likely just tread water — broad equity exposure is the steadier bet.

gold.caveat: Gold can pull back sharply, dragging the gold-linked bundle down with it.

clean_factors.test: r_i = a + b_mkt·MKT_exMonsoon + b_rain·RURAL_f ; genuine gate b_rain>0 & |t|>=2
clean_factors.method: FWL orthogonalized market control (MKT_exMonsoon) + RURAL_f factor; HAC t
clean_factors.spurious_note: Per the naive-vs-clean test: a name is GENUINE only if it loads positively + significantly (|t|>=2) on RURAL_f AFTER the clean MKT_exMonsoon market control. Names that looked monsoon-linked under the naive (RURAL_f+NIFTY) test but lose significance under the clean control are SPURIOUS (market beta, not rural).
clean_factors.control_factor: MKT_exMonsoon (market with Auto + FMCG sectors purged)
clean_factors.mechanical_loading_note: 73 of 82 'genuine' names are RURAL_f CONSTITUENTS — their ~+1 loading on RURAL_f is MECHANICAL (circular self-loading), so they confirm the thesis basket but are NOT independent evidence. Only 9 names load on RURAL_f significantly WITHOUT being part of it (Asian Paints, Titan, Page, Jubilant, SRF…) — these are the real cross-sectional discoveries: urban-discretionary/quality names that genuinely co-move with rural demand.

expressions.plain_label: High-payoff bet on the rural leader
expressions.plain_one_liner: A small, defined-risk bet that pays several times your money if the move happens — but you can lose all you put in.
expressions.plain_why: Options give a big, convex payoff for a small outlay when the move is large enough.
expressions.plain_risk: You can lose 100% of what you put in if the move doesn't happen in time.
expressions.option_legs_note: A defined-risk 'call spread' — your loss is capped at what you pay. Exact strikes are set when you deploy.
expressions.exit_period: Held to expiry over the window

option_model.assumptions: Modelled with Black–Scholes at the underlying's realised volatility and a stated risk-free rate on a reference spot of 100; final strikes and premia are set at deploy. Max loss is capped at the debit paid.

monsoon.plain_thesis: We looked at past seasons with an above-normal monsoon. In the 6 months after each, an equal bundle of rural-demand names — tractors, fertilisers, two-wheelers and FMCG — beat the Nifty in most of them. The catch: rainfall forecasts change late, and a market-wide fall still drags the bundle down.
monsoon.description: We looked at past seasons with an above-normal monsoon. In the 6 months after each, an equal bundle of rural-demand names — tractors, fertilisers, two-wheelers and FMCG — beat the Nifty in most of them. The catch: rainfall forecasts change late, and a market-wide fall still drags the bundle down.
bullets: What drives it: a good monsoon lifts farm income and rural spending.
How to act: own an equal bundle of 6 rural-demand companies.
Main caveat: forecasts shift late in the season — the signal is noisy.

yes.summary: A good monsoon means better farm income, and the tractor, fertiliser, two-wheeler and FMCG names that sell into it tend to rise together.

no.summary: A weak monsoon squeezes rural spending — these names usually lag, so broad equity exposure is the steadier bet.

monsoon.caveat: If the whole market falls, the bundle usually falls too.
